entries: Project development｜read the script or program goal and determine the audience, genre, and delivery format｜mark undecided creative and commercial assumptions.
Production preparation｜list budget, schedule, locations, personnel, and rights needs｜make no external commitments before approval.
Creative design｜the director sets the shot, performance, and sound direction; the producer checks resource feasibility｜keep versions for changes.
On-set execution｜coordinate actors, camera, lighting, sound, and safety staff｜execute high-risk scenes under a professional plan.
Material review｜check picture, sound, continuity, authorizations, and missing items｜record pickup or revision decisions.
Delivery and distribution｜check the final version, the contract's scope of use, and the delivery channel｜keep approvals and the material list.

Workplace｜office, set, stage, recording, or post-production locations vary with the project.

description.text: Producers and directors are responsible for the creation and production coordination of stage, film, television, broadcast, and video works. See the O*NET 27-2012 tasks, 2025 United States wages, the BLS 2025–2035 projection, the Chinese wage evidence gap, and the fictional entry exercises.

subject.name: Producers and directors
subject.summary: Producers and directors plan and coordinate stage, television, radio, video, or film productions. Producers focus on resources, budget, contracts, and delivery, while directors focus on creative decisions such as script interpretation, performance, camera, and sound; both must communicate with the team and check safety, rights, and versions.
